headline: Samsung has reportedly passed final quality checks for its newest AI memory chip, with Nvidia and big cloud firms likely customers.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered to 6: the qualification was completed in late September, so the event is stale, and Samsung has not confirmed the report.
importance_line: What changed: if confirmed, Samsung would be ready to supply this memory, which matters to AI chip makers and the cloud firms that buy them, but the report is unconfirmed, the buyers are unnamed, and passing tests does not guarantee orders or volumes.
summary: Hankyung reports, as relayed by Sammy Fans, that Samsung finished qualification in late September for its 12-layer HBM4E, a stacked memory chip used with AI processors, which means it met key customers' technical and reliability requirements. Nvidia and large cloud companies are widely considered the likely customers, but Samsung has not confirmed the report or named them, and there is no information yet on supply volumes or mass production dates.
notes: Event before 7 Oct (qualification completed late Sep); first reported 7 Oct. URL is the Sammy Fans page where the text was read; the Hankyung original was not opened. KED Global (chunk source) headline only.
